newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss private bank bullish on Eastern Europe.
newsitem.headline: Swiss private bank bullish on Eastern Europe.

text.p: Geneva's Union Bancaire Privee expects growth to pick up in Eastern Europe's emerging economies in 1997, led by Poland, its January monthly outlook said.
"With an expected Gross Domestic Product growth rate of five percent per annum till the end of this century, this region stands out as the future powerhouse of Europe," it said.

The bank forecast Polish GDP growth at six percent in 1997, up from 1996's estimated 4.7 percent, driven by high investments and stronger exports in response to an expected increase in Russian demand and Western businesses.
Hungary's GDP, recovering from tough belt-tightening, should grow by 2.5 percent in 1997 after 1996's one percent as investments and exports pick up and demand stabilises, it said.
Russia should also grow in 1997 after years of hefty output falls, said the bank, predicting two percent Russian GDP growth.
The bank was gloomy on the Czech Republic, where it said the economy was deteriorating into overheating and the risk of a currency devaluation loomed as a possibility.
Union Bancaire Privee saw enormous potential for the region's stock markets, propelled by sustained economic progress, strong earnings growth, declining interest rates and rising foreign interest.
Despite last year's market rallies, Polish and Hungarian stocks still remained attractively valued with multiples of around 8.5 times the 1997 earnings estimates, the bank said.
